label: web-design-guidelines
summary: An audit of a finished page's code against the Web Interface Guidelines: accessibility, focus, reduced motion. The third skill `page-design` applies, and the one whose findings win a disagreement.
why: No API key and no paid product. The skill holds no rules: it fetches them from GitHub on every run, so it does not work offline and the rules can change between two runs. With no network `page-design` reports the audit as not run. Installing runs the third-party `skills` CLI through npx, which needs Node.js 22.20 or later.

install.run: npx -y skills@latest add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines -a claude-code -y
install.note: `npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines -a claude-code` is the example in the `skills` CLI README; `-y` (skip prompts) is from its docs/commands.md (both read 2026-11-13). One run is on record, on 2026-11-13, through `cckit doctor --fix` in a Next.js project: the skill landed in .claude/skills/web-design-guidelines and skills-lock.json was written; whether .agents/skills/ got a copy was not recorded. Per the CLI's docs it installs into the current project (`-g` would make it global): a copy under .agents/skills/, a link at .claude/skills/web-design-guidelines, and an entry in skills-lock.json.

verify.failsOn: The skill file is in neither this project nor ~/.claude/skills. A file check only: it does not prove the rules can be fetched.

afterInstall: reload the agent session so it lists the skill, and commit .claude/skills/web-design-guidelines, skills-lock.json and .agents/skills/web-design-guidelines when it exists

drifts: the package name skills on npm and its `add` options --skill, -a, -y
the skill folder name web-design-guidelines in vercel-labs/agent-skills
the rules URL the skill fetches: raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md
